issues.description: Public API surface narrowed without a deprecation cycle on a published format class
issues.detail: NAME, QUANTIZED_VECTOR_COMPONENT, calculateDefaultConfidenceInterval, and the Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsReader constructor go from public to package-private in one shot. Anything downstream that was using these (and there are real users of Lucene99 scalar quant) gets a compile break on upgrade, not a deprecation warning. State the policy: either keep them @Deprecated public for one release, or document the break in CHANGES.txt under Backward Compatibility Breaks.

issues.description: fieldsWriter throws UnsupportedOperationException instead of being structurally absent
issues.detail: Making a writer that exists only to throw at runtime is the wrong shape. If the format is read-only, the type system should say so (separate read-only base, or no KnnVectorsFormat registration of the write side). A user who configures this format in an IndexWriter now learns at flush time, not at config time. At minimum, the exception message should name the replacement format Lucene104HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat.

issues.description: Patch does three things; should be three patches
issues.detail: This single diff: (1) physically moves files to backward_codecs, (2) tightens visibility on numerous symbols, (3) removes the writer path and the unused numMergeWorkers/mergeExec fields, (4) adds RW test shims and renames an existing one. Each is reviewable; the bundle is not. Split: pure move + service registration first, visibility tightening second, writer removal third. Reviewer-six-months-from-now bisecting a regression will curse this commit.

issues.description: @Deprecated annotation dropped from the moved format classes
issues.detail: The old classes were @Deprecated in core; after the move the annotation is gone. They are still deprecated in intent (legacy, read-only, replaced by Lucene104). Keep @Deprecated so IDEs and javac warn users who still instantiate them. Removing it sends the opposite signal from CHANGES.txt.

issues.description: protected fields demoted to package-private on a non-final public class with public subclass
issues.detail: OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues is public and DenseOffHeapVectorValues extends it publicly. Flipping the protected fields to package-private works because the subclass sits in the same package, but it forecloses any out-of-package extension of this public abstract class. If that is intended (because it is moving to backwards_codecs and we do not want extension), make the class final or sealed; if not, keep protected. Pick one.

issues.description: Dead-code removal of numMergeWorkers/mergeExec changes constructor semantics silently
issues.detail: The constructors still accept numMergeWorkers and ExecutorService and still validate them, but the values are now discarded. Callers passing a real executor get no error and no effect. Either ignore the parameters via @Deprecated overloads that document the no-op, or remove the validating branches that now guard nothing meaningful. Half-removing the feature is the worst of both worlds.

review.summary: The move-to-backwards-codecs is the right direction and most of the mechanical work is fine: file relocations, module-info, and SPI registration all line up. What's wrong is shape. This is three patches stapled together (move, visibility tightening, writer removal), it silently breaks any downstream caller of formerly-public symbols without a deprecation cycle, and it leaves a writer method that throws at runtime instead of expressing read-only-ness in the type system. The @Deprecated annotation got dropped on classes that are absolutely still deprecated. NEEDS-WORK: split the patch, restore deprecation markers, decide whether the writer path exists or not, and document the API breaks in CHANGES.txt.
